author: Josh Ayen
title: TinCaps hold off Great Lakes in extra innings for 5th straight win - NewsBreak
text:
By Josh Ayen ,
1 hours ago
MIDLAND, Mich. (WANE) – The TinCaps extended their winning streak to five games following Wednesday’s 5-4 win over Great Lakes that was decided in 10 innings.
With the win, Fort Wayne is over .500 for the first time in the second half of the Midwest League season. The TinCaps are also closing the gap in the East Division standings, trailing first place Great Lakes by two games following Wednesday’s results.
Wednesday’s game was a pitcher’s duel through the first five innings. Both the TinCaps and Loons kept the game scoreless until the sixth inning. Kasen Wells broke the deadlock in the sixth frame with a 2-out RBI single, scoring Rosman Verdugo. Lamar King Jr. doubled the TinCaps’ lead in the seventh inning with another 2-out RBI single, driving in Alex McCoy to make it a 2-0 game.
Great Lakes got both runs back in the bottom of the seventh frame to tie the game at 2-2. Neither side could score over the final two innings, resulting in a 10th inning. The TinCaps pulled off clutch hitting in the extra frame. King delivered his second RBI of the night with a single to left field, bringing in Jack Costello for the go-ahead run. Kasen Wells and Justin DeCriscio followed that up with an RBI single apiece to give the TinCaps a 5-2 lead midway through the extra inning.
The Loons nearly forced an 11th inning, getting two runs back on a base hit from Nico Perez. However, Winyer Chourio retired three straight batters to finish off a gutsy win for Fort Wayne.
Chourio earned his second win since being promoted to Fort Wayne. The flamethrower pitched the final five innings of Wednesday’s game, allowing four runs on six hits and one walk. He also fanned eight batters, including the game-sealing out in the 10th inning.
The TinCaps go for their sixth straight win Thursday at Great Lakes. First pitch is 7:05 p.m. at Dow Diamond.
